actionRequired.description:
Give terminal phase correctly to all pods that will not be restarted. 

In particular, assign Failed phase to pods which are deleted while pending. Also, assign a terminal 
phase (Succeeded or Failed, depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) to pods which
are deleted while running.

This fixes the issue for jobs using pod failure policy (with JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions 
feature gates enabled) that their pods could get stuck in the pending phase when deleted.

Users who maintain controllers which relied on the fact that pods with RestartPolicy=Always
never enter the Succeeded phase may need to adapt their controllers. This is because as a consequence of 
the change pods which use RestartPolicy=Always may end up in the Succeeded phase in two scenarios: pod 
deletion and graceful node shutdown.

securityInformation.title: Bypassing enforce mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityInformation.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using ephemeral containers. The policy ensures pods running with a service account may only reference secrets specified in the service account's secrets field. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if the ServiceAccount admission plugin and the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation are used together with ephemeral containers.

**Note**: This only impacts the cluster if the ServiceAccount admission plugin is used (most cluster should have this on by default as recommended in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#serviceaccount), the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation is used by a service account (this annotation is not added by default), and Pods are using ephemeral containers.

issueContext.title: An option to disable Preferred Inter-pod affinity of existing pods
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

An option in the scheduler's ComponentConfig to ignore calculating preferences of exiting pods' affinity rules for the general case, and consider them only if the incoming pod has inter pod affinities.  In most cases this is sufficient because pods set inter-pod affinity against each other.

In the past we optimized this case by tracking only pods with inter-pod affinity, but to achieve the next level of scheduling throughput, optionally disabling this feature will be useful.

Specifically, I am suggesting that [PreScore](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3e26e104bdf9d0dc3c4046d6350b93557c67f3f4/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/scoring.go#L126) exits early if this option is enabled and the pod has no inter-pod affinities.

### Why is this needed?

To optimize for higher scheduling throughput.

/sig scheduling

/cc @Huang-Wei @alculquicondor

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/

#### What happened:

Names allowed for Pods, Deployment, StatefulSet follow DNS subdomain name defined in RFC 1123. 
Pods controlled by Deployment follows DNS subdomain name standard as well. 

However, Pod controlled by StatefuSet is following DNS label standard.
StatefulSet allows names with "." , but Pods created by the StatefulSet fails with error --

```
Events:
  Type     Reason        Age                     From                    Message
  ----     ------        ----                    ----                    -------
  Warning  FailedCreate  4m23s (x17 over 9m51s)  statefulset-controller  create Pod sts1-vol.1-0 in StatefulSet sts1-vol.1 failed error: Pod "sts1-vol.1-0" is invalid: spec.hostname: Invalid value: "sts1-vol.1-0": a DNS-1123 label must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters or '-', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'my-name',  or '123-abc', regex used for validation is '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?')
```


#### What you expected to happen:

Since "." character is allowed in the StatefulSet name, Pod replicas controlled by the StatefulSet should allow "." character as well. 
If "." is not possible for Pods controlled by StatefulSet, then StatefulSet creation should fail for "." character in the name. 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```
$ kubectl create -f 1sts-1vol-dot.yaml -n test
persistentvolumeclaim/pvc-3 created
statefulset.apps/sts1-vol.1 created
```

issueContext.title: kube-scheduler: Bring back the ability to stop at the first failed filter
issueContext.body:
#108829 changed the default behavior of scheduler framework's `RunFilterPlugins` - from stopping at the first failed filter to always running all filters. This change breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale. Cluster Autoscaler imports the scheduler framework to simulate filters on artificial nodes. In a (pretty common) one-pod-per-node scenario, the number of `RunFilterPlugins` calls is ~quadratic wrt. the number of nodes needed for unschedulable pods - it can be a lot of calls. Before #108829, in such scenario the vast majority of `RunFilterPlugins` calls would stop at failing Fit or NodeAffinity filters, and not run the rest of them (e.g. PV-related filters). After the change, every call to `RunFilterPlugins` runs all filters, which completely breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale (an example scenario of 300 1-pod-per-node pods and 200 node groups takes >10min in 1.24, and ~50s in <1.22).

Can we get the old behavior back? Or re-introduce the config option so that Cluster Autoscaler can set it accordingly? Ideally, we'd also like to get this backported as far as possible (the change was introduced in 1.24).

### What would you like to be added?

The go-jose dependency version should be updated from v2.2.2 to v2.6.0.

### Why is this needed?

This is to make the kubernetes code compatible with newer go-jose v2 versions that have a small breaking change: `jwt.NewNumericDate()` returns a pointer in newer versions which breaks the kubernetes code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0-alpha.2/pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go#L93):
```
/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/kubernetes@v1.26.0-k3s1/pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go:93:29: cannot use jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(time.Duration(warnafter) * time.Second)) (value of type *jwt.NumericDate) as type jwt.NumericDate in assignment
```
For instance this prevents using the kubernetes apiserver and [ory/fosite](https://github.com/ory/fosite/tree/v0.44.0) together within the same Go codebase.

issueContext.title: informers: provide a way to know when a resource handler has "synced"
issueContext.body:
Currently, informers expose a `HasSynced` method.
This asserts that one full List has been synced to the informers *store*.

However, this does not give any guarantees about *handlers* being called.

It is fairly common to need to know that the handlers have been called for the initial state.
However, there is currently no way to access this.

Slack context: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1591115369066700

## Sync state

A common question is "What happens if an object is created during the initial sync? Why would we care about the initial state specifically?"

The issue is one of eventually consistency. If I apply, say, a NetworkPolicy, it may not be actuated for some time - its perfectly reasonable for a controller to not process it for O(seconds). However, if I apply a NetworkPolicy 1 year ago, then restart my controller, it *must* be applied; a small blip in policy enforcement is a CVE. A correct controller implementation needs to ensure the initial state is fully synced before operating.

* The naive option is to just use `informer.HasSynced`. ### What happened?

When submitting a windows pod using resource limits on a node with more than one processor group, the specified `CpuMaximum` count is incorrect due to the usage of `runtime.NumCPU()` which does not take processor groups into account.

For example:
- node with 96 cores
- cpu limit 94
- `runtime.NumCPU()` returns `48`

This results in a CPU maximum of 10000 since the range is from [1, 10000]:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container_windows.go#L82..L91

```go
	limit := int64(94 * 1000)
	numCPU := 48
	fmt.Println(((10000 * limit) / int64(numCPU) / 1000))

// Output:
// 19583
```

Our initial goal for this was to limit a process to not use all available CPU and therefore render the node uncontrollable. 

### What did you expect to happen?

A CPU maximum of `9791` instead of `10000` for that specific case. For the calculation, it should use the CPU count for all available processor groups instead of just the current one.

issueContext.title: Reading from secret volume occasionally fails with `permission denied`
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Reading files from secret volume fails with `permission denied` because files incorrectly have group owner GID 0 instead of given `fsGroup`. Failure happens only occasionally and if checking the volume manually after the error, the problem has disappeared and the files can be read successfully. The problem started after applying file permissions `defaultMode: 0440` to the secret volume and the security context with `fsGroup: 10000`. The process that reads the files is NOT running with UID 0 or GID 0.

issueContext.body:
The ipvs mode `ipvs-scheduler` limit the scheduler algorithm to :
```
              rr - Round Robin: distributes jobs equally amongst the available real servers.

              wrr - Weighted Round Robin: assigns jobs to real servers  proportionally  to  there
              real  servers'  weight.  Servers with higher weights receive new jobs first and get
              more jobs than servers with lower weights. Servers with equal weights get an  equal
              distribution of new jobs.

              lc - Least-Connection: assigns more jobs to real servers with fewer active jobs.

              wlc  -  Weighted Least-Connection: assigns more jobs to servers with fewer jobs and
              relative to the real servers' weight (Ci/Wi). This is the default.

              lblc - Locality-Based Least-Connection: assigns  jobs  destined  for  the  same  IP
              address to the same server if the server is not overloaded and available; otherwise
              assign jobs to servers with fewer jobs, and keep it for future assignment.

              lblcr - Locality-Based Least-Connection with Replication: assigns jobs destined for
              the  same  IP  address  to  the  least-connection node in the server set for the IP
              address. If all the node in the server set are over loaded, it picks up a node with
              fewer  jobs  in  the  cluster  and  adds it in the sever set for the target. If the
              server set has not been modified for the specified time, the most  loaded  node  is
              removed from the server set, in order to avoid high degree of replication.

              dh  -  Destination Hashing: assigns jobs to servers through looking up a statically

issueContext.title: Deletecollection failing after 34 seconds
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In a cluster with large enough numbers of objects, it seems to be impossible to clean them up with `deletecollection`.  Because the deletecollection is failing while listing the objects from etcd.  The failure happens after exactly 34 seconds, due to the 34-second max timeout introduced in PR #96901 (cc @tkashem for insight on that PR).



### What did you expect to happen?

The deletecollection should be able to run for longer, and succeed.

I recognise that there are still risks of the API server using too much RAM, if deleting a very large collection due to issue #90743.  But, until _that_ issue is fixed, it seems like allowing `deletecollection` to run for longer might be a good idea.  As far as I can tell, the 34 second timeout does not apply to normal LIST calls, so on that basis I feel it should not apply to the giant unchunked LIST call that happens inside `deletecollection`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a few hundred thousand objects of some particular type.  (Argo workflowtaskresults happen to be the type I'm looking at while I write this)
2. Call deletecollection. (Optionally passing some kind of fieldSelector, but I don't think that's essential)

issueContext.title: CSI migration race condition can cause unexpected detach and data loss
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

After the cluster was updated to enable PD CSI Driver, there was a race condition where AD Controller (kube-controller-manager) started to [populate the desired state of world](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dc2898b20c6bd9602ae1c3b51333e2e4640ed249/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L438-L447) BEFORE the PD CSI Driver was up, thus AD Controller gave us the error 

```
Error creating spec for volume "elasticsearch", pod "XXX"/"elasticsearch-0": error performing CSI migration checks and translation for PVC "dXX"/"elasticsearch-elasticsearch-0": in-tree plugin kubernetes.io/gce-pd is migrated on node gke-stage-XXXXX but driver pd.csi.storage.gke.io is not installed.
```

Then AD Controller triggered the disk detach because the disk/volume was not populated in the desired state of world.

Unfortunately the disk was in use during this detach and got corrupted.

### What did you expect to happen?

Since cluster upgrades can cause the controller manager and CSI drivers to start at different times, the AD controller needs to be more conservative when detaching

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We have not been able to reproduce this, it came up from a customer.

issueContext.title: Cacher may not send events if it reinitializes at the time of watch initialization
issueContext.body:
Found when reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116024

I'm still not 100% convinced it's true, but I believe this is a faulty scenario:
1. new watch is being established `Watch()` method
2. `c.ready` is still initialized so we successfully pass the c.ready.wait() check
3. `ListAndWatch` in `startCaching` fails (for whatever reason)
4. `c.ready.set(false)` is called (from defer in `startCaching`)
5. `startCaching` is called again and we call `terminateAllWatchers()`
6. the Watch call (started in point 1 above) only now continues to be processed and is established (and added to watchers) - init events are being send in the meantime
7. `ListAndWatch` is being called from `startCaching` which reinitializes watchCache to a new (higher RV)
8. if some events missed in the meantime, they will not be delivered to this newly established watch

/kind bug
/priority critical-urgent
/sig api-machinery

issueContext.title: Enforce ReadWriteOncePod PVC access mode during scheduling
issueContext.body:
See [KEP-2485](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/2485-read-write-once-pod-pv-access-mode) for more context.

#### What would you like to be added:

The `ReadWriteOncePod` PVC access mode guarantees only a single pod can access the provided PVC as a volume. This is enforced during volume mount (in kubelet), and should be additionally enforced during scheduling.

#### Why is this needed:

Because without it the scheduler will assign pods to nodes and they will fail to start (due to failed volume attachment / mount).

#### Implementation details:

- The `NodeInfo` type will be extended to store a mapping of PVC names to the number of pods on the node consuming that PVC
- The `VolumeRestrictions` scheduler plugin is extended to have a lister for PVC and for `NodeInfo`
- During PreFilter, the plugin enumerates each `NodeInfo` checking the reference count for each PVC in the pod to be scheduled
- If the pod to be scheduled's PVC is using the `ReadWriteOncePod` access mode and that PVC is found with a reference count > 0, mark the pod `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` (alpha)
  - For beta, we will mark the pod `Unschedulable` and implement preemption logic

issueContext.title: dynamic resource allocation: ensure PrepareResources called before CNI invoked
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Ensure that `PrepareResources()` is called against all DRA `kubelet` plugins for all containers before CNI is invoked.

This can be done by either moving this call earlier in the process of doing pod creation, or moving it into the `PodAdmission` loop (as is done by the existing device plugin framework).

Ideally, we would follow the pattern used by the existing device plugin. This would allow us to integrate seamlessly with the `TopologyManager`, for example, for DRA kubelet plugins that wished to do so.

However, there are unfortunate issues with this approach. The biggest one being that there is no retry loop for transient failures when calling out to external plugins. This means that if a transient failure does occur, the pod fails admission with an `UnexpectedAdmissionError` (even though it could have quickly recovered with a subsequent call out to the plugin, for example. Other resource managers, beyond DRA (especially the device plugin) could also benefit from improving the situation around transient failures, so this approach is worth exploring

The alternate approach, i.e. simply moving the `PrepareResources()` earlier in the process if pod creation is fairly straightforward, and a PR for doing so has already been created:
* https://github.com/pohly/kubernetes/pull/43

However, this doesn't allow us to integrate as nicely with the other resource managers, as moving it to the pod admission loop would.

We will need to consider what the right approach is as we start to work on this.

### Why is this needed?

This link summarizes the reasons behind needing this enhancement well:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111023#discussion_r1005306039

Quoted from that review comment:
> The PrepareResources is called after the CNI is invoked. This is a problem for network devices that want to use DRA framework.
>
> In our case we have complex netdevice with several of other devices that we want to map

issueContext.title: [E2E] Support for pulling images from private registry
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Our team is using sonobuoy to run the conformance tests on a cluster. When running Sonobuoy E2E/Conformance tests, deployed pods will go into an ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff state when the image resides in a repository that requires authentication, and credentials are not passed with the request.

The [E2E/Conformance test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e) process spawns pods in separate namespaces to run E2E/Conformance tests. If pods are referencing images from a private registry, the secrets wouldn’t be available in the newly created namespaces and the pod will fail to start.

This is the issue reported by one of the sonobuoy users - https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/issues/1038

Kubernetes E2E framework provides a `--e2e-docker-config-file`  flag which takes in a file containing the credentials that can be used to pull images from private registries needed for a test.  Using the credentials a secret can be created in the newly created namespace. 
With the Secret created, the default service account (in the new namespace) will be patched with the created secret and can then be referenced by the test pod, and repository authentication should be successful.


### Why is this needed?

As of now, when running the E2E tests, the flag is only being checked in a single test - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/57eb5d631ccd615cd161b6da36afc759af004b93/test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go#L292-L308
so despite passing the credential file, other tests would fail.

The `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` sysctl is namespaced so should be safe to permit. It is an often necessary counterpart to `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` sysctl which is currently in the default safe list. It would therefore be helpful to include it in the default safe list as well.

### Why is this needed?

If you have a pod with multiple containers which both sets the `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to a large range such as the commonly used '1025 65535' in order to maximise the number of available ports *and* binds to local ports in that range then it is possible for a container doing a bind to deadlock repeatedly failing to start if the another container has already used the local port as an ephemeral port. If the ports needed by the bind can be added to the reserved ports list then this issue can be avoided without having to unnecessarily shrink the local port range or add coupling to ensure containers start in the correct order to prevent the deadlock.

issueContext.body:
#### What would you like to be added:

Make node affinity and tolerations mutable for Jobs. 

#### Why is this needed:

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97170 we added a new flag to allow suspending jobs to control when the Pods of a Job get created by controller-manager. We proposed this as a primitive that higher-level controllers can use to support job queuing,

Allowing to mutate node affinity and tolerations allows a higher-level queue controller to influence job placement by injecting node affinity or tolerations before un-suspending a job.

The implementation is basically relaxing the validation on job updates to allow for mutating the node affinity and tolerations of the pod template for jobs.

/sig scheduling

feature.description: Since Kubernetes v1.5, `kubectl apply` has had an alpha-stage `--prune` flag to support deleting previously applied objects that have been removed from the input manifest. This feature has remained in alpha ever since due to performance and correctness issues inherent in its design. This PR exposes a second, independent pruning alpha powered by a new standard named `ApplySets`. An `ApplySet` is a server-side object (by default, a Secret; ConfigMaps are also allowed) that kubectl can use to accurately and efficiently track set membership across `apply` operations. The format used for `ApplySet` is set out in  [KEP 3659](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3659) as a low-level specification.  Other tools in the ecosystem can also build on this specification for improved interoperability.  To try the ApplySet-based pruning alpha, set `KUBECTL_APPLYSET=true` and use the flags `--prune --applyset=secret-name` with `kubectl apply`.

This is a new major release of kustomize, so there are a few backwards-incompatible changes, most of which are rare use cases, bug fixes with side effects, or things that have been deprecated for multiple releases already:

- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4911: Drop support for a very old, legacy style of patches. patches used to be allowed to be used as an alias for patchesStrategicMerge in kustomize v3. securityFixes.title: Bypassing enforce mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using ephemeral containers. The policy ensures pods running with a service account may only reference secrets specified in the service account's secrets field. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if the ServiceAccount admission plugin and the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation are used together with ephemeral containers.

**Note**: This only impacts the cluster if the ServiceAccount admission plugin is used (most cluster should have this on by default as recommended in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#serviceaccount), the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation is used by a service account (this annotation is not added by default), and Pods are using ephemeral containers.

bugOrRegression.description: Adds an opt-in mitigation for http/2 DOS vulnerabilities for CVE-2023-44487 and CVE-2023-39325 for the API server when the client is unauthenticated. The mitigation may be enabled by setting the `UnauthenticatedHTTP2DOSMitigation` feature gate to `true` (it is disabled by default). An API server fronted by an L7 load balancer that already mitigates these http/2 attacks may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to avoid disrupting load balancer → kube-apiserver connections if http/2 requests from multiple clients share the same backend connection. An API server on a private network may choose not to enable the kube-apiserver mitigation to prevent performance regressions for unauthenticated clients. Authenticated requests rely on the fix in golang.org/x/net v0.17.0 alone. https://issue.k8s.io/121197 tracks further mitigation of http/2 attacks by authenticated clients.
